questions.question: When driving in heavy traffic, you should:

options.text: Use hands-free cell phone devices.
Text on your cell phone instead of calling.
Not use your cell phone.
Turn up the volume on your cell phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not use your cell phone.
questions.explanation: Heavy traffic requires your full attention. You must avoid all distractions, including using your cell phone.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: 10 feet of your vehicle.
1,000 feet of your vehicle.
Your view of the road ahead.
A minute of hitting the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: You must stop your vehicle within the distance you can see ahead. Slow down when you cannot see far enough down the road.

questions.question: If a vehicle has a vehicle inspection report, the driver should:

options.text: Not look at the report and instead find any issues themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Review the report.
Not do a pre-trip inspection and rely only on the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the report.
questions.explanation: Always read the last inspection report for your vehicle. Any problems listed should have been fixed by the owner.

questions.question: When backing, it is best to:

options.text: Only use the passenger side mirror.
Back up quickly.
Turn toward the passenger side whenever possible.
Use a helper, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper, if possible.
questions.explanation: When backing up, go slowly and use both side mirrors. Always use a helper to watch your blind spots if you can. Agree on a stop signal before you start.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when rain first starts to fall?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Roads are naturally slippery.
Gravel washes to the middle of the lane.
Tires are not designed for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first begins, it mixes with oil and grease already on the road, creating a slick surface. As more rain falls, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: To leave a stop as safely as possible, you should park:

options.text: So that you must back up to leave.
So that you can pull forward to leave.
On the side of a roadway, not in a parking lot.
By backing into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: So that you can pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous. Park in a way that lets you pull forward to exit your space whenever possible.

questions.question: One way to handle blind spots is to:

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so they cannot pass you.
Stay in the left lane and only watch vehicles on your right.
Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are.
Avoid using your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see the traffic around you. This helps you notice when other vehicles move into your blind spots.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer will continue in a straight line.
The trailer will disengage.
The trailer will likely swing around.
The trailer will stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will likely swing around.
questions.explanation: When trailer wheels lock up, the trailer tends to swing around. This can cause a jackknife.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver on the road, you should:

options.text: Follow their vehicle closely.
Try to get their attention.
Give them plenty of room.
Flash your lights at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give them plenty of room.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance from distracted drivers. Be careful when passing them because they may not see you and could drift into your lane.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment:

options.text: The parking brake should not be engaged.
Wheels should be chocked.
The engine should be running.
The gearshift should be in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wheels should be chocked.
questions.explanation: Before checking the engine compartment, set the parking brake and block the wheels. Check the engine before starting it.

questions.question: What is the easiest way to know your trailer is skidding?

options.text: Ask another driver.
Check your mirrors to see if the trailer left its lane.
Release the brake pedal and push it down again.
Watch the jackknife warning light on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors to see if the trailer left its lane.
questions.explanation: The easiest way to spot a trailer skid is to use your mirrors. When you brake hard, check your mirrors to make sure your trailer is still in the correct position.

questions.question: What does eating while driving do?

options.text: Saves time.
Is a good idea on long trips.
Takes your attention away from driving.
Is required to keep cargo supervised.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid driving distracted, do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Anything that takes your attention away from driving is a distraction.

questions.question: Why is backing up with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo might fall out of the trailer.
There might be extra weight in the front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you must back up, use a helper if possible.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.
Press the accelerator.
Tap the accelerator twice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a yellow diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to turn on the parking brakes and push it in to turn them off.

questions.question: Where are the ABS warning lights located on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the driver's door.
On the instrument panel.
On the outside of the vehicle near the passenger door.
Under the hood.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the instrument panel.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with ABS have yellow warning lights on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS warning lights on the left side, at the front or rear corner.

questions.question: What is one function of the emergency air line?

options.text: Control the emergency brakes.
Flash when air pressure is too low.
Allow for quick turning.
Control steering in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Control the emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (or supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: If your pre-trip inspection finds something unsafe, what should you do?

options.text: Continue driving and schedule a mechanic appointment after the trip.
Let a more experienced driver use the truck.
Get it fixed right away.
Avoid using the unsafe items but continue driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get it fixed right away.
questions.explanation: If a pre-trip inspection finds something unsafe, you must have it repaired immediately. It is illegal to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ than driving a single vehicle.

options.text: Is easier.
Requires more skill.
Is better for training.
Is safer in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires more skill.
questions.explanation: Driving a combination vehicle usually requires more skill than driving a single vehicle because combination vehicles are longer and heavier.

questions.question: After you finish a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Close the service line valve.
Remove the service line valve.
Leave the emergency line valve open.
Leave the rear shut-off valves open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the service line valve.
questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check that air reaches all the brakes. Close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: What is true about doubles and triples?

options.text: They turn easily due to their center of gravity.
They are harder to turn than smaller commercial vehicles.
They should never be turned.
They always have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to turn than smaller commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because they are so large, doubles and triples cannot turn quickly. They need extra care when turning to avoid tipping over.
